Finally, it is a deed unworthy and most alien not only to any religious man, but even to any honorable Christian, which that Brother <term>Romanus</term>, wandering so often among the Cretans, has marked out against <term>Crusius</term>; for in order to convict him of falsehood, he has admitted as many crimes of falsity as he will be deservedly forced to blush for, once convicted by the public instrument completed at Cologne by <term>Crusius</term>, unless perhaps he has already turned completely pale in his coffin, or has worn away his entire forehead against the gateposts of that <term>Hortus</term>. <term>Crusius</term> produces witnesses, corrupted neither by envy nor favor, jurists of the most perfect reputation, to whose eyes, faith, and public declarations, issued in such number and with such diligence, no prudent person could deny belief, who affirm that the allegations of <term>Crusius</term>, with the places compared with their authors, are sincere and uncorrupted, which you, by badly introducing moles into the <term>Hortus</term> and with secret grasping, have tried in vain to tear down.
